findings.description: These predicates now use the raw escaped keyword for JSON-text columns, deleting the conversion that was specifically added so Chinese searches match Unicode-encoded JSON stored in the database. Workflow runs are still persisted with ordinary `json.dumps`, so searching for `中文` now builds `%中文%` while the row contains `\u4e2d\u6587`, and the matching log is omitted. Use a separately Unicode/JSON-encoded and LIKE-escaped pattern for `WorkflowRun.inputs`/`outputs`, while retaining the raw pattern for `EndUser.session_id`.
findings.failureMode: Searching workflow logs by Chinese or other non-ASCII text present in inputs or outputs returns no matching run.
findings.title: Keep JSON Unicode encoding for log search

findings.description: `escape_like_pattern` prefixes `%`, `_`, and `\` with backslashes, but this SQL declares `|` as the only LIKE escape character. With `IRIS_TEXT_INDEX` disabled, searching for literal `50%` therefore sends `%50\%%`: a row containing `50%` does not match because the query requires a backslash, while `%` still acts as a wildcard. Use backslash in the ESCAPE clause (as the helper requires), or transform the pattern with `|`.
findings.failureMode: IRIS fallback full-text searches containing `%`, `_`, or `\` return missing or unrelated documents.
findings.title: Match the IRIS escape character to the pattern

findings.description: Unlike the three sibling branches, this `notlike` omits `escape="\\"` after transforming `%`, `_`, and `\` into backslash escape sequences. On a supported MySQL deployment using `NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES`, an omitted ESCAPE clause means there is no escape character, so a filter such as metadata `not contains "50%"` interprets the `%` as a wildcard (and the inserted backslash literally) and returns the wrong document set. Pass the same explicit escape argument used by the other conditions.
findings.failureMode: On MySQL with NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES, a `not contains` metadata filter containing a LIKE metacharacter includes or excludes the wrong documents.
findings.title: Declare the escape character for `not contains`

findings.description: For a one-key request such as `GET foo`, the `<=` iteration runs again with `j == numkeys`; the zero-initialized spare reference selects `argv[0]` (`GET`), whose slot differs from `foo`, so an ordinary request is rejected as CROSSSLOT. The same iteration always writes `slot_buffer[numkeys]` beyond the allocated buffer (and for larger results can also read beyond `keys`), introducing heap corruption/crashes. Iterate only while `j < keys_result->numkeys`.
findings.failureMode: Ordinary key-bearing cluster commands can return spurious CROSSSLOT errors, and every such extraction performs an out-of-bounds heap write that can corrupt or crash the server.
findings.title: Stop slot extraction at `numkeys`

findings.description: This new `malloc`/`free` scratch buffer violates the repository's mandatory requirement that allocations in `src/` use `zmalloc`/`zfree`, so the temporary memory is omitted from Redis allocator accounting on every key-bearing cluster command. The slot array is never read, so remove the scratch allocation and its frees rather than bypassing the tracked allocator.
findings.failureMode: Cluster command preprocessing performs an allocation invisible to Redis's required allocator tracking.
findings.title: Remove the direct libc allocation

findings.description: `TEAM_MEMBER` is the minimum role in `TEAM_ROLES`, and `RolesGuard` allows a role whose index is at or above that minimum; consequently an ordinary accepted MEMBER can call this endpoint and mint a team-wide invitation token. This contradicts the admin-only contract and the added member test (which will receive 200 instead of 403). Use `@Roles("TEAM_ADMIN")`, as the existing organization invite endpoint does.
findings.failureMode: Any ordinary team member can generate shareable team invitations, bypassing the endpoint's admin authorization requirement.
findings.title: Require team-admin authorization for invite creation

findings.description: `ResponseInterceptor` is registered globally and JSON-serializes every controller result into `responseBody`. This new response includes `inviteLink`, whose query contains the valid random invitation token (and, after correcting the token field, `data.token` too), so creating a regular-team invite persists its reusable join credential in application logs. Redact these fields at the logging sink or opt this response out of body logging.
findings.failureMode: Anyone able to read application logs can extract a live invite token and use it to join a team without receiving the intended share link.
findings.title: Keep invitation bearer tokens out of response logs

findings.description: For every new invite this returns `invite-link-for-teamId-${teamId}` (the identifier), while the database redemption path and `inviteLink` use the random `token`. The response token therefore cannot redeem the invite, is identical across repeated requests for one team, and already makes both invite endpoint suites fail. Return `newToken.token` (or the local `token`).
findings.failureMode: A successful create-invite call returns an unusable and repeated token that differs from the one in its invite URL.
findings.title: Return the persisted invite token

findings.description: The condition was inverted: a regular team (`isOrgContext === false`) now gets a `/signup?...callbackUrl=...` link, while an organization or org sub-team gets `/teams?token=...`. This swaps the established flows for both supported contexts; restore `if (!isOrgContext)` so regular teams use `/teams` and org contexts use signup/onboarding.
findings.failureMode: Every newly generated invite link sends regular-team and organization invitees through the wrong acceptance flow.
findings.title: Restore invite routing for each team context

findings.description: This direct `@calcom/features` import is explicitly forbidden for API v2 and Biome reports it as an error, so the required lint gate fails. Import the already-exported service from `@calcom/platform-libraries`, matching the existing organization invite controller and API v2 package dependencies.
findings.failureMode: The changed files cannot pass the repository's required Biome lint gate.
findings.title: Import TeamService through the API v2 boundary

findings.description: This `.e2e-spec.ts` suite relies on test globals and is selected only by API v2's Jest configuration; that runner is also invoked without `TZ=UTC`. It therefore bypasses the repository mandate that all added tests use Vitest under UTC. Port/import the Vitest APIs and include the suite in the standardized UTC test run.
findings.failureMode: The new endpoint coverage is not exercised by the repository's mandated Vitest/UTC test environment.
findings.title: Run the new endpoint suite under Vitest in UTC

findings.description: The controller's manually wrapped Nest import/method and the missing trailing newline in `teamService.ts` do not match the repository's mandated Biome format; the formatter check exits nonzero on these two changed files. Apply Biome formatting to both before merging.
findings.failureMode: A Biome formatting verification of the changed TypeScript files fails.
findings.title: Format the changed TypeScript files with Biome

findings.description: The rewritten command contains seven objects (`HSETEX key KEEPTTL FIELDS 1 field value`) but declares an argc of 6. rewriteClientCommandVector consumes only `argc` varargs, so the retained/propagated command ends at `field`; HSETEX rejects it for lacking the value. This leaves replicas stale, and with AOF enabled the increment is silently lost after restart (a repro returned 2.1 before restart and 1 afterward). Set the rewritten argc to 7.
findings.failureMode: Every successful HINCRBYFLOAT propagation/AOF record omits the new value, leaving replicas stale and silently losing the increment on AOF restart.
findings.title: Pass the full seven-argument HSETEX vector

findings.description: For an existing volatile field, this local update now omits HASH_SET_KEEP_TTL. hashTypeSet explicitly persists an existing field whenever that flag is absent (for both listpack-ex and hash-table encodings), so `HSETEX h EX ...; HINCRBYFLOAT h f ...` makes HTTL return -1 on the primary. Meanwhile the rewritten replica command is specifically intended to keep its old TTL, creating the opposite primary/replica divergence. Restore HASH_SET_KEEP_TTL on this hashTypeSet call.
findings.failureMode: An ordinary HINCRBYFLOAT against a volatile hash field removes the field expiration on the primary and diverges from its replica.
findings.title: Preserve the TTL on the primary update too

findings.description: This change drops `static` from addHashFieldToReply even though every source reference remains in t_hash.c. That grants an internal implementation function external linkage and directly violates the repository mandate that single-file helpers use static storage; restore the deleted qualifier.
findings.failureMode: The changed source violates the mandatory internal-helper encapsulation rule by granting external linkage to a file-local helper.
findings.title: Keep the reply helper file-local

findings.description: The `== '1'` operator enables BUILD002 precisely for the first servicing patch, while the repository still carries its 9.0 baseline. A concrete example is `Microsoft.AspNetCore.AzureAppServices.HostingStartup`: that baseline contains `System.Text.Json`, but the current project no longer references it, so building 10.0.1 now reports the unsuppressible BUILD002 and fails. After advancing to 10.0.2, the same operator disables this servicing guard altogether. This transition gate must be `!= '1'`, as in the upstream change, so patch 1 can build and later servicing patches retain the check.
findings.failureMode: The current 10.0.1 build fails BUILD002 against stale 9.0 references (and 10.0.2+ would stop checking removed references entirely).
findings.title: Invert the patch-one gate on BUILD002

findings.description: Both pools were moved to macOS-15, but their setup commands still select `/Applications/Xcode_15.2.0.app`; only the display labels were updated. The macOS-15 image provides Xcode 16.x (with 16.4 at `/Applications/Xcode_16.4.0.app`) and no 15.2 bundle, so both public and internal macOS jobs exit in this setup step before the build. Update both command paths to 16.4, as intended.
findings.failureMode: Every macOS build using either branch of this template fails in `xcode-select` because `/Applications/Xcode_15.2.0.app` does not exist on macOS-15.
findings.title: Select the Xcode version installed on macOS 15

findings.description: The servicing baseline manifest assigns `10.0.25.52413` to all 141 managed assemblies, but the released `Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Ref` 10.0.0 package contains `10.0.25.52411`; the repository's own release-branch instructions require copying this file from that RTM package. Shipping this pre-RTM/dummy manifest makes SDK conflict resolution reason about framework files newer than those actually present and can incorrectly prune a package asset whose file version falls between the two. Replace these entries with the RTM manifest (52411), as the immediate upstream correction did.
findings.failureMode: A servicing targeting pack reports every managed framework file at a nonexistent newer file version, allowing framework/package conflict resolution to select or prune assets against the wrong baseline.
findings.title: Use the released 10.0.0 file versions in the platform manifest

findings.description: The branch now sets `PreReleaseVersionLabel` to `servicing`, but the replacement mapping only handles alpha, preview, rc, and rtm. Consequently `PreReleaseBrandingLabel` is empty and prerelease installer display names are emitted as e.g. `10.0.1 Build ...` rather than `10.0.1 Servicing Build ...`. Add the missing `servicing` → `Servicing` condition.
findings.failureMode: All non-stabilized 10.0.1 servicing installers are produced with incomplete product display names that omit the Servicing branding.
findings.title: Define branding for the servicing label

findings.description: This changes the only C# file in the diff from a file-scoped namespace to a block-scoped namespace, contrary to the repository's mandatory rule that all C# files use file-scoped declarations. A compliance/style validation of this changed file will reject it; keep `namespace Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.E2ETests.ServerExecutionTests;` and remove the new trailing namespace brace.
findings.failureMode: The changed C# source fails the repository's namespace compliance requirement/check because it now uses a brace-delimited namespace.
findings.title: Restore the required file-scoped namespace

findings.description: The `|| iPad()` condition suppresses theme restoration for all iPad onboarding tests, although only bottom placement is unsupported there. When `testFirstRunTourDarkMode` runs on an iOS 17+ iPad, it selects dark and this broad condition prevents resetting light; the theme manager writes that selection to `UserDefaults.standard`, and the UI-test reset does not clear UserDefaults, so later cases inherit the wrong theme. Restrict this exception to the unsupported bottom-placement/iPad combination.
findings.failureMode: On an iOS 17+ iPad, `testFirstRunTourDarkMode` persists dark theme and teardown takes the broad iPad branch instead of restoring light, contaminating subsequent UI tests.
findings.title: Do not skip theme restoration for every iPad test

findings.description: The permission alert is presented asynchronously after the Paste action, but this new handler waits only 0.5 seconds for existence and then taps without checking hittability. On a loaded simulator/device, an alert that appears later is skipped (or one mid-presentation is tapped while not hittable), after which the URL bar never receives the clipboard value and every caller times out in `mozWaitForValueContains`. Use the normal test timeout and wait for the SpringBoard alert button to be hittable, as the repository's other paste-alert handlers do.
findings.failureMode: If iOS takes more than 0.5 seconds to present the Allow Paste prompt, copy/share UI tests time out because the prompt remains unanswered and the pasted URL never appears.
findings.title: Wait for the paste permission alert to become tappable

findings.description: This `return` exits before `app.terminate()` and `super.tearDown()`. Thus the newly skipped iPad bottom-placement case (and, with the current condition, bottom placement on iPhone and every iPad case) leaves Firefox running and bypasses the XCTest cleanup chain; when that is the last selected case the test run completes with the app still active. Skip only the theme-reset operation and then fall through to the unconditional cleanup.
findings.failureMode: Run `testSelectBottomPlacement` alone on an iOS 17+ iPad: the test is skipped, this return is taken, and the launched Firefox process is never terminated by teardown.
findings.title: Always run the teardown cleanup

findings.description: Changing the method's prefix from `test` to `verify` removes it from XCTest discovery, so FullFunctional/direct runs silently stop exercising the bookmark-to-Reminders flow even though the method still contains assertions and the helper below is being stabilized for it. This also violates the repository's explicit test-method naming contract. Restore the `testBookmarksShareNormalWebsiteReminders` name.
findings.failureMode: When ShareLongPressTests is executed, XCTest does not register the `verify...` method, so a broken bookmark-to-Reminders flow produces no test failure.
findings.title: Keep the reminder check discoverable as a test

findings.description: The broad `|| iPad()` branch also matches `testFirstRunTourDarkMode`, which explicitly selects the dark manual theme. On an iOS 17+ iPad its teardown now skips the prior light-theme restoration; that selection is stored in UserDefaults and `ClearProfile` does not clear UserDefaults, so later tests can run with the wrong dark appearance. Exempt only the skipped flow that cannot navigate to Appearance, not all iPad onboarding tests.
findings.failureMode: Run testFirstRunTourDarkMode on an iOS 17+ iPad followed by a test expecting the default light theme; the first test leaves the persisted manual theme dark and the later test sees the wrong appearance.
findings.title: Do not suppress theme restoration for every iPad test

findings.description: Renaming this XCTest method from `testBookmarksShareNormalWebsiteReminders` to a `verify...` name removes it from XCTest discovery, so the bookmark-to-Reminders flow is silently never executed even though the method and assertions remain. This also violates the repository's explicit test-method naming contract. Restore the `test` prefix (and fix flakiness in the helper independently).
findings.failureMode: When ShareLongPressTests are discovered, XCTest omits the bookmark Reminders case entirely, so regressions in that flow pass CI unchecked.
findings.title: Keep the bookmark reminder method discoverable as a test

findings.description: For `testSelectBottomPlacement` on iPhone and every onboarding test on iPad under iOS 17+, this `return` exits before both `app.terminate()` and `super.tearDown()`. Running any such case leaves the application under test alive after the case and bypasses the base XCTest cleanup. Guard only `switchThemeToDarkOrLight`, then fall through to the common teardown.
findings.failureMode: After an affected iOS 17+ onboarding case completes or skips, Firefox remains running and the BaseTestCase/XCTest teardown chain is not executed.
findings.title: Always run teardown cleanup

findings.description: A path cannot have both the `json` and `json5` extension, so this `&&` makes schema validation unreachable for every file. This also removes a safety boundary: the schema forbids `/` in `productName`, while Serde only deserializes that field; on macOS the bundler appends `.app`, treats an absolute product name as an absolute path, and recursively removes an existing directory there. For example, `"productName": "/tmp/victim"` can make `tauri build` delete `/tmp/victim.app`. Restore `||`.
findings.failureMode: On macOS, build a JSON config with an absolute `productName` such as `/tmp/victim` while `/tmp/victim.app` exists; schema validation is skipped and bundling recursively deletes that unrelated directory.
findings.title: Keep JSON schema validation reachable

findings.description: `bundle` is an object, while the required bundle identifier is the root-level `identifier`; therefore the new `as_str()` chain yields `None` for every valid config. All Android and iOS build/dev paths call `write_options`, which turns that `None` into `app configuration is missing an identifier`, so normal mobile commands now fail before launching. Restore the root `identifier` lookup.
findings.failureMode: With any normal config such as `{ "identifier": "com.example.app", "bundle": {} }`, `tauri android build/dev` and `tauri ios build/dev` fail while writing CLI options because `original_identifier()` is `None`.
findings.title: Keep reading the root identifier

findings.description: The hunk removes `config_metadata.inner = serde_json::from_value(value).context("failed to parse config")?;`, so the freshly merged `value` is discarded and only extension metadata is updated. Starting from a loaded config with no product name, `merge_with({"productName":"changed"})` returns `Ok` but the returned handle still exposes `None`; restore the deserialization/assignment before inserting the extension.
findings.failureMode: Load a config and then call `merge_with` with a valid CLI override; callers receive success but reads through the returned `ConfigHandle` keep the pre-merge settings, so the requested override is ignored.
findings.title: Apply merged values to the live config

findings.description: The required `cargo fmt --all -- --check` command rejects both this new validator line and the new `extensions.insert` line at 289. Apply rustfmt so the repository's formatting check can pass.
findings.failureMode: The mandated Rust formatting check exits nonzero on the changed source.
findings.title: Format the changed Rust code

findings.description: `TEAM_MEMBER` is the minimum role, and `RolesGuard` orders OWNER, ADMIN, MEMBER then permits any role at or above that index. Consequently an authenticated ordinary MEMBER can call this endpoint and create shareable invitation credentials for the team, contrary to the endpoint's admin-only contract (and the added 403 test). Use `@Roles("TEAM_ADMIN")`.
findings.failureMode: An ordinary team member posts to `/v2/teams/:teamId/invite` and receives a newly generated invite instead of 403, bypassing the intended team-admin authorization boundary.
findings.title: Require the team-admin role

findings.description: For every newly created invite, this returns `newToken.identifier` (the predictable value `invite-link-for-teamId-${teamId}`) while `inviteLink` embeds the random `token`. The API therefore returns a value that cannot be used to redeem the invite and is not contained in the link; the newly added success and uniqueness assertions fail. Return `newToken.token` (or the local `token`) instead.
findings.failureMode: A successful invite request returns an unusable, non-unique token and a mismatched inviteLink/token pair on the mainline path.
findings.title: Return the generated verification token

findings.description: This condition is inverted relative to the existing context contract: it now sends organizations and organization sub-teams to `/teams`, while regular teams are sent to the organization-oriented `/signup?...callbackUrl=...` flow. For example, an unauthenticated recipient of an organization invite is redirected by `/teams` to login rather than the org-aware signup flow, so a prospective new org member cannot use the advertised link. Keep `/teams` for `!isOrgContext` and build the signup link for org context.
findings.failureMode: Generated invite links route both regular-team and organization recipients through the wrong onboarding flow; in particular, new organization invitees are sent to login instead of signup.
findings.title: Restore invite routes for each team context

findings.description: This direct `@calcom/features` import is explicitly forbidden in API v2 by the repository's `noRestrictedImports` rule, so the required lint gate exits with an error. `TeamService` is already exposed through `@calcom/platform-libraries` and the existing organization invite controller imports it from that facade; use the allowed export here.
findings.failureMode: CI/pre-commit lint fails on the new controller, preventing the change from passing the repository gate.
findings.title: Import TeamService through the platform facade

findings.description: The response schema unconditionally says that `inviteLink` opens `/signup`, although this endpoint supports both regular teams and organization contexts and their established flows differ: regular-team links use `/teams?token=...`, while organization-context links use signup. Thus even after the independent branch inversion is corrected, Swagger still publishes the wrong behavior/example for every regular-team response. Describe both context-dependent routes and use examples that do not claim signup is universal.
findings.failureMode: Generated API documentation gives regular-team consumers the wrong route and onboarding behavior for inviteLink.
findings.title: Document both invite-link routes

findings.description: The replacement command has seven arguments (`HSETEX`, key, `KEEPTTL`, `FIELDS`, count, field, value), but `rewriteClientCommandVector` is told to consume only six, so `newobj` is omitted. The emitted `HSETEX key KEEPTTL FIELDS 1 field` is rejected for lacking a value, so replicas and AOF reloads skip every acknowledged `HINCRBYFLOAT`; a restart or replica promotion loses those increments. Pass an argc of 7.
findings.failureMode: Execute any successful HINCRBYFLOAT with AOF or replication enabled, then restart from that AOF or promote the replica: the malformed propagated HSETEX is not applied and the acknowledged increment is lost.
findings.title: Include the value in the rewritten HSETEX vector

findings.description: For an existing field with a TTL, `HINCRBYFLOAT` now calls `hashTypeSet` without `HASH_SET_KEEP_TTL`, whose documented behavior is to discard that TTL. The rewritten `HSETEX ... KEEPTTL` only controls propagation, so the primary/standalone server loses the expiry while replicas preserve their prior expiry; the field consequently persists on the primary after it has expired on replicas. Keep `HASH_SET_KEEP_TTL` on this local mutation.
findings.failureMode: Run HSETEX with a future expiry and then HINCRBYFLOAT on that field: HTTL becomes -1 on the executing server, while a replica applying the rewritten HSETEX retains the expiry and later deletes the field.
findings.title: Preserve the field TTL on the executing server

findings.description: This change exports `addHashFieldToReply` even though every reference remains within `t_hash.c` and there is no public declaration. That directly violates the repository mandate that internal helpers use static storage and adds an unintended global linker symbol; restore the deleted `static`.
findings.failureMode: The built object exposes `addHashFieldToReply` globally despite it being file-local, failing the repository's mandatory internal-helper encapsulation requirement.
findings.title: Keep the file-local reply helper static

findings.description: The migrated list response declares `availability[].days` as `string[]`, but the server's Prisma `Availability.days` field and `getScheduleListItemData` both use `number[]`. When `useAtomGetAllSchedules` passes its result to `getScheduleListItemData` in the list-schedules atom, TypeScript rejects the mainline build because a schedule containing `string[]` is not assignable to that transformer's `number[]` contract. Declare this field as `number[]`, matching the handler return that was replaced.
findings.failureMode: Building/type-checking the atoms schedule list fails at the unchanged `getScheduleListItemData(schedule)` call due to `string[]` versus `number[]`.
findings.title: Keep availability day values numeric

findings.description: The broadened restriction now rejects every `@calcom/trpc/**` import, but two atoms components still import `@calcom/trpc/components/QueryCell`. Running the targeted restricted-import lint across the atoms package checks 170 files and exits nonzero with exactly these two errors, so the new enforcement and the source tree disagree. Replace those remaining dependencies as part of the decoupling rather than merging a package that fails its own restriction.
findings.failureMode: Biome's package-wide `noRestrictedImports` check exits with two errors because the newly broadened restriction matches dependencies still present in atoms.
findings.title: Remove remaining imports before enforcing the package-wide ban

findings.description: Both migrated ID fields are declared as strings even though the live slot implementation produces numeric database user IDs: the removed `Slot.userIds` contract was `number[]`, and the `IFromUser.id` carried through OOO slot metadata is `number`. Consumers of the newly exported `Slot` contract or the public `useAvailableSlots` result therefore cannot type-check correct numeric-ID handling, while string-only handling is accepted against runtime numbers. Change `Slot.userIds` to `number[]` and `SlotInfo.fromUser.id` to `number`.
findings.failureMode: An atoms consumer that handles `userIds` or OOO `fromUser.id` as the numeric IDs actually returned fails to build; string methods accepted by the declaration receive numbers at runtime.
findings.title: Preserve numeric IDs in slot response types

findings.description: The new validator uses single-quoted literals despite the repository's mandatory double-quote Biome configuration. Running Biome 2.3.10's formatter validation on this changed file exits nonzero and identifies lines 39–46; format these literals before merging.
findings.failureMode: Biome formatter validation exits with status 1 on `hooks/schedules/types.ts` because the changed literals are not in the configured format.
findings.title: Format the new TypeScript with Biome

findings.description: `result.get("result")` is `str | None`, and the guard explicitly permits `None` before returning it from a method declared to return `str`. The registered `make type-check` command fails with `reportReturnType` on this changed line. Reject every non-string value with `TemplateRenderError` so the implementation actually returns `str`.
findings.failureMode: The mandatory backend type-check command exits nonzero at this return, blocking the required check.
findings.title: Reject `None` to satisfy the renderer contract

findings.description: The newly added assertion puts the constant on the left, triggering Ruff SIM300. The repository's registered `make check` command exits with an error on this changed line, so the lint gate fails until the operands are reversed.
findings.failureMode: Running the registered backend check fails with SIM300 at this assertion.
findings.title: Fix the lint-breaking reversed assertion

findings.description: Setting `strict` to false disables `strictNullChecks`, but the installed TanStack Router types explicitly require it. Running the registered `tsc -b --noEmit` check at this head fails across the app with errors such as `Argument ... is not assignable to parameter of type '"strictNullChecks must be enabled in tsconfig.json"'`; `npm run build` invokes the same project build and will fail before Vite. Restore `strict: true` and fix the new components' types instead of bypassing strict checking.
findings.failureMode: Both the required type-validation command and the production UI build fail because a dependency rejects compilation without strict null checking.
findings.title: Do not disable strict mode required by the router types

findings.description: This always binds the status to `trigger.expect`, and `work-queue-status-trigger-fields.tsx:36` does the same. A rendered-form check confirms that choosing Proactive/“Stays in” and Paused produces `expect: ["prefect.work-pool.paused"]` with no `after`. After a Paused event, the trigger then waits for another Paused event and ignores Ready/Not Ready transitions, so it can fire even though the resource has already left Paused. Bind the selected status to `trigger.after` for Proactive posture, as the deployment and flow-run templates do.
findings.failureMode: A Proactive work-pool or work-queue status automation can fire after the resource leaves the selected status because other status events do not satisfy its incorrectly narrow `expect` filter.
findings.title: Store proactive pool and queue statuses in `after`

findings.description: `split("\n")` always returns at least one element, and a rendered-form check confirms that typing and then clearing this textarea writes `expect: [""]`. The backend treats a genuinely empty `expect` as matching any event, but a set containing the empty string does not satisfy `expects()` for real event names; the saved reactive automation therefore never reaches its threshold although the UI shows no filter. Detect an empty value (and discard blank lines) before calling `field.onChange`.
findings.failureMode: Clearing the custom expected-events textarea silently creates an impossible empty-string event filter, so the automation does not fire for real events.
findings.title: Do not serialize a cleared event list as an empty event name

findings.description: The new proactive “Within” inputs all advertise `min={0}` (also at deployment line 99 and pool/queue line 96), while the backend rejects Proactive windows from 1 through 9 seconds. A focused parse confirms the wizard schema accepts `posture: "Proactive", within: 1`, so the Trigger step advances and later produces a payload the API rejects. Set these inputs to a 10-second minimum and add posture-aware schema validation so typed values cannot bypass it.
findings.failureMode: A Proactive trigger configured with a 1–9 second window passes wizard validation but fails automation creation with a backend validation error.
findings.title: Enforce the proactive ten-second minimum

findings.description: This `Number(...)` conversion (also used by the new deployment and work-queue fields) stores decimal values unchanged. A rendered input check produced `threshold: 1.5`, and the Zod wizard schema accepts it, but the backend `EventTrigger.threshold` contract is an integer; automation creation will therefore reject the payload. Validate thresholds as integers (preferably in the schema) instead of allowing fractional values through the Trigger step.
findings.failureMode: Entering a fractional threshold in the custom, deployment, or work-queue template passes front-end validation but causes the automation request to fail backend validation.
findings.title: Reject fractional event thresholds

findings.description: Wrapping the Radix `Select` root in `FormControl` does not put the generated form-item id on the rendered trigger button, and these new `SelectTrigger`s have no id or accessible label. Consequently clicking “Status” does not focus/open the control and `getByLabelText("Status")` cannot find it; screen-reader users encounter an unnamed combobox. Put `FormControl` around `SelectTrigger` (or add matching id/`aria-label`) in all three status components.
findings.failureMode: The Status dropdowns for deployment, work-pool, and work-queue templates cannot be identified or activated via their visible labels by assistive technology or label-click interaction.
findings.title: Associate each Status label with its select trigger

findings.description: The repository requires every React component to have a same-directory `component.test.tsx`. None of the four new components has its corresponding `custom-trigger-fields.test.tsx`, `deployment-status-trigger-fields.test.tsx`, `work-pool-status-trigger-fields.test.tsx`, or `work-queue-status-trigger-fields.test.tsx`; the modified `trigger-step.test.tsx` only checks that labels render and does not satisfy the mandated filenames. Add the four co-located test files, including assertions for the values each field writes.
findings.failureMode: The change fails the repository's mandatory React test-layout compliance and leaves the new form serialization behavior outside its required component test targets.
findings.title: Add co-located tests for each new trigger component

findings.description: The new comparison is inverted for the current transition: `AspNetCorePatchVersion` is 1 while the checked-in package baseline is still 9.0, so this enables BUILD002 precisely when it must be skipped. Building `Microsoft.AspNetCore.AzureAppServices.HostingStartup` now fails because that stale baseline still lists `System.Text.Json`, which the current project correctly no longer references. Change this comparison to `!= '1'`; that lets the initial servicing build proceed and keeps the reference-removal check active on later patches instead of disabling it there.
findings.failureMode: Any build including Microsoft.AspNetCore.AzureAppServices.HostingStartup fails with BUILD002 for removed System.Text.Json on the new 10.0.1 configuration, preventing the servicing branch from building.
findings.title: Fix the inverted patch-version check

findings.description: Both macOS pools are moved to the macOS-15 image, but their setup step still executes `xcode-select` against `/Applications/Xcode_15.2.0.app`; only the display names were changed to 16.4. The macOS-15 hosted image exposes Xcode 16.x (including `/Applications/Xcode_16.4.0.app`) and not 15.2, so every public or internal macOS job using this template fails in setup before the build. Update both `xcode-select` paths along with the image/display name.
findings.failureMode: A macOS job starts on macOS-15 and `sudo xcode-select -s /Applications/Xcode_15.2.0.app/Contents/Developer` exits nonzero because that developer directory is absent.
findings.title: Select the Xcode version installed on macOS-15

findings.description: `AspNetCorePatchVersion` now identifies 10.0.1, but this disables `EnsureBaselineIsUpdated` while the checked-in baseline still identifies 9.0.0. Consequently dependency changes introduced in 10.0 are absent from `BaselinePackageReference`; removing one in 10.0.1 can pass without BUILD002 and ship a breaking servicing-package dependency change. No replacement for this guard is visible in the diff (one may be planned separately), so generate the 10.0.0 baseline and keep validation enabled until replacement enforcement lands.
findings.failureMode: A 10.0.1 shipping project removes a package dependency that existed in 10.0.0 but not 9.0.0; because the stale 9.0 baseline is permitted, `UnusedBaselinePackageReference` never contains it and BUILD002 does not stop the servicing build.
findings.title: Do not bypass the stale package-baseline guard

findings.description: The new servicing baseline manifest records the placeholder file version `10.0.25.52413` for the managed shared-framework assets, while the released Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Ref 10.0.0 manifest records `10.0.25.52411`; this was subsequently identified upstream as “dummy values from pre-RTM build.” The SDK loads these values into platform conflict resolution and chooses the higher file version, so an app carrying an intermediate/newer package asset can have that asset removed on the false premise that the 10.0.0 shared framework contains 52413. Copy the manifest from the released 10.0.0 targeting pack.
findings.failureMode: When a package contributes one of these assemblies at file version 10.0.25.52412, conflict resolution treats the declared platform version 52413 as the winner and removes the package asset, although an RTM machine actually supplies only 52411; the application then runs against the older assembly rather than its package asset.
findings.title: Use the released 10.0.0 platform file versions

findings.description: `PreReleaseVersionLabel` is now `servicing`, but the replacement branding map defines values only for alpha, preview, rc, and rtm. As a result `PreReleaseBrandingLabel` is empty and `BrandingVersionSuffix` becomes only `Build ...`, so servicing installers/packages lose the expected `Servicing` branding. Add the servicing mapping used by release branches (for example `<PreReleaseBrandingLabel Condition="'$(PreReleaseVersionLabel)' == 'servicing'">Servicing</PreReleaseBrandingLabel>`).
findings.failureMode: Any non-stabilized 10.0.1 servicing build evaluates `PreReleaseBrandingLabel` to empty and emits human-facing branding without the servicing designation.
findings.title: Define branding for the servicing label

findings.description: This changed declaration converts the C# file from a file-scoped namespace to a block-scoped namespace, directly violating the repository's mandatory source-file rule. Restore `namespace Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.E2ETests.ServerExecutionTests;` (the quarantine attribute does not require changing namespace form) so the file passes repository compliance review.
findings.failureMode: The changed C# source is rejected by the repository's mandatory compliance check/review because it now uses a traditional namespace block.
findings.title: Retain the required file-scoped namespace

findings.description: `handleShowReaderModeAction` processes `showReaderMode`, which the middleware dispatches for an ordinary reader-mode button tap, but it now selects `.readerModeLongPressAction`. `BrowserViewController` handles that by creating a Reading List record; it never calls `toggleReaderMode()`. Restore `.readerMode` so the tap enables/disables reader mode instead of unexpectedly saving the page.
findings.failureMode: On a reader-compatible page, tapping the reader-mode toolbar button adds the page to Reading List and leaves reader mode unchanged.
findings.title: Reader-mode taps add the page to Reading List

findings.description: Reversing these values changes the argument fed to `readerModeButtonTapped`, whose existing implementation stores `isEnabled` in the `is_private` extra. Consequently, closing reader mode in a normal tab (`.active`) is now recorded as private, and opening it in a private tab (`.available`) is recorded as non-private. It also makes the unchanged default-state test fail: the nil reader state takes `default: true`, so `savedExtras.isPrivate` is true instead of the asserted false. Restore the prior true/false mapping; the older argument-order defect is separate.
findings.failureMode: Reader-mode telemetry is assigned to the wrong privacy cohort for reachable active-normal and available-private taps, and the existing middleware test fails for its default nil state.
findings.title: Reader telemetry now mislabels browsing mode

findings.description: `selectedTab.url` is the raw `http://localhost/.../reader-mode/page` URL while reader mode is active, whereas `displayURL` decodes it back to the article URL and normal URL updates deliberately dispatch that value. By accepting reader-mode URLs here, a tabs/menu/cancel action sends the raw URL into `handleCancelEditAction`, replacing the address-bar state's public article URL. Keep excluding reader URLs as before or dispatch `currentURL.displayURL`.
findings.failureMode: While viewing an article in reader mode, invoke a toolbar action that calls `cancelEditMode` (for example Menu); the address bar changes from the article URL to Firefox's internal localhost reader URL.
findings.title: Canceling edit exposes the internal reader-mode URL

findings.description: This implementation-only dependency had `private` access and still has no caller outside `ToolbarTelemetry`, but the change gives it implicit internal visibility. That violates the repository mandate requiring explicit, minimally appropriate access control on every property and exposes the raw metric-recording interface module-wide. Restore `private let` so this file passes the mandatory compliance review.
findings.failureMode: The changed Swift file fails mandatory access-control compliance: `gleanWrapper` lacks an explicit modifier and is exposed beyond the only type that uses it.
findings.title: Keep the Glean wrapper private

findings.description: After `Action.SelectLightTheme`, this reads `darkThemeView` and immediately expects it to be selected. The production view tracks exactly one selected option and exposes `"1"` only for that option, so selecting Light leaves this queried Dark value at `"0"` and the test fails before checking the remaining modes. Query `lightThemeView` here.
findings.failureMode: Running `DisplaySettingTests/testCheckSystemThemeChanges` against a correctly functioning Appearance screen fails the first assertion after selecting Light.
findings.title: Check the light theme element after selecting Light

findings.description: Moving this navigation after the `Done` tap means `Done` is now requested while the test is still on the directly pushed `TopSitesSettingsViewController`. That controller configures its title but no `Done` button; `Done` belongs to its parent homepage/root settings controllers. The preceding `waitAndTap()` therefore times out before this line or either assertion can run. Navigate back out of the subpage before dismissing Settings, preserving the prior sequence.
findings.failureMode: Running `HomePageSettingsUITests/testDisableTopSitesSettingsRemovesSection` reaches the Shortcuts settings screen and fails waiting for a nonexistent Done button.
findings.title: Leave the Shortcuts subpage before tapping Done

findings.description: Deleting `checkCopiedUrl()` here leaves the subsequent paste-and-assert flow guarded by `if #available(iOS 17, *)`. On the supported iOS 15 path, `testClipboard` now copies the URL, creates a tab, performs no clipboard assertion, and passes even when Copy writes the wrong value. Retain this call or add an equivalent pre-iOS-17 assertion.
findings.failureMode: Run `ClipBoardTests/testClipboard` on iOS 15 with a regression that leaves the pasteboard unchanged after tapping Copy; the test reports success instead of detecting the broken copy behavior.
findings.title: Keep clipboard validation on iOS 15

findings.description: The changed declarations on lines 11, 17, and 41 make helper methods `public`, although repository-wide search shows they are used only inside `ClipBoardTests` (and `checkCopiedUrl` has no live caller). This directly violates the repository's mandatory rule against marking internally used implementation details public. Mark all three helpers `private`.
findings.failureMode: The change fails the repository's mandatory access-control compliance review because file-local test helpers are declared public.
findings.title: Do not expose file-local clipboard helpers

findings.description: Setting `strict` to false also disables `strictNullChecks`, but TanStack Router's types explicitly require it. The repository's `npm run validate:types` now emits errors such as `Argument ... is not assignable to parameter of type 'strictNullChecks must be enabled in tsconfig.json'` across router consumers, so the required type-validation/build path fails. Restore `strict: true` and fix any errors in the new fields rather than disabling it globally.
findings.failureMode: The main UI type-validation job fails because dependencies reject a project compiled without strict null checks.
findings.title: Keep `strictNullChecks` enabled for the UI build

findings.description: Both the work-pool selector and the identical work-queue selector bind every status choice to `trigger.expect`, even when the posture is Proactive (“Stays in”). The backend therefore treats the selected status as the event whose absence is being tested and leaves `after` empty, so entering that status does not start the persistence window. For Proactive, put the selected status in `after` and the other status events in `expect`; retain the selected status in `expect` only for Reactive.
findings.failureMode: A Proactive pool/queue automation configured as “Stays in Ready” tests for missing Ready events instead of timing how long the resource remains Ready, producing the opposite trigger behavior.
findings.title: Build proactive pool and queue status criteria in `after`

findings.description: The deployment selector changes which field it edits based on posture, but a selection updates only that one field and never clears or recomputes the now-hidden criterion. For example, choose Reactive/Ready, switch to Proactive, and choose Ready again: the payload has both `after: [ready]` and `expect: [ready]`. A transition to Not Ready then does not satisfy `expect`, so the automation can fire claiming the deployment stayed Ready even though it left that state. Build both fields consistently on posture/status changes—selected status in `after` and its complement in `expect` for Proactive, with stale `after` removed for Reactive.
findings.failureMode: After changing posture, a deployment status automation retains a hidden status criterion and can fire for a state the deployment has already left.
findings.title: Clear stale status criteria when posture changes

findings.description: `"".split("\n")` returns `[""]`, so `lines.length > 0` is always true. After a user enters a custom event and then clears the textarea, the form therefore submits `expect: [""]` instead of an empty/undefined list. The server accepts this value, but `expects()` is false for every real event, leaving the resulting automation unable to trigger. Filter blank lines and set the field to undefined (or surface required validation) when none remain.
findings.failureMode: Clearing the custom-events textarea produces a trigger expecting the impossible empty-string event, so the saved automation never fires.
findings.title: Do not serialize a cleared event list as an empty event name

findings.description: All four newly exposed Proactive forms render `within` with `min={0}`, and the local trigger schema likewise accepts every nonnegative value. The server rejects proactive windows from 1 through 9 seconds (only zero is normalized to its default). For example, entering 5 passes the wizard's trigger-step validation but the create/update API returns 422. Enforce the 10-second proactive minimum in both the input and cross-field form validation.
findings.failureMode: Entering a proactive `within` value between 1 and 9 seconds is accepted by the UI but rejected by the automation API, so submission fails.
findings.title: Reject proactive windows below the API minimum

findings.description: The deployment, work-queue, and custom threshold handlers preserve fractional values via `Number(...)`, while the wizard's `z.number().min(1)` accepts them. Next invokes only the resolver via `form.trigger(...)`, so entering `1.5` advances and reaches the output payload even though the server's `int` threshold rejects it. Make threshold validation integral (the work-pool handler already truncates, though explicit integer validation would avoid silently changing input).
findings.failureMode: A fractional threshold such as 1.5 passes the trigger step but is rejected by the API as `int_from_float`, so the automation cannot be saved.
findings.title: Validate integer thresholds before advancing

findings.description: During normal boot, `emailAnalytics.init()` executes this changed require, but the checkout still contains only `EmailEventStorage.js`. On a case-sensitive production filesystem Node throws `MODULE_NOT_FOUND`, so Ghost startup fails. Point this require back to the existing filename, or include the corresponding file rename.

findings.title: Restore the actual EmailEventStorage module path

findings.description: Once the preceding storage import is fixed, normal `emailAnalytics.init()` reaches this changed require, but the tree has only `EmailEventProcessor.js`. On case-sensitive production filesystems it throws `MODULE_NOT_FOUND`, so Ghost startup still fails. Use the existing filename or add the omitted rename.
findings.failureMode: Normal Ghost boot calls EmailAnalyticsServiceWrapper.init(), which throws MODULE_NOT_FOUND for ../email-service/email-event-processor after the storage import is fixed.
findings.title: Restore the actual EmailEventProcessor module path

Normal boot calls `members.init()`, which loads the members API and throws `MODULE_NOT_FOUND` on a case-sensitive filesystem, preventing Ghost startup.
