findings.failureMode: Normal Ghost boot calls members.init(); its members API load throws MODULE_NOT_FOUND for ../../lib/magic-link/magic-link.
findings.title: Keep the existing MagicLink filename

findings.description: The nine changed declarations on lines 1–10 omit their terminating semicolons. `ghost/core` extends `plugin:ghost/node`, whose pinned shared rules configure `semi: ['error', 'always']`, so `yarn lint:server` fails on this file. Restore all nine semicolons.
findings.failureMode: The required server lint fails with missing-semicolon errors for the nine changed declarations.
findings.title: Restore required semicolons on imports

findings.description: `result.get("result")` is `str | None`, but this branch returns it from a method declared to return `str`. Both repository type-checkers reject the changed file at this line (`uv run --dev basedpyright ...` and the CI Mypy command each exit nonzero), so the style gate cannot pass. Treat `None` as an invalid result and raise `TemplateRenderError`, or otherwise ensure a string before returning.
findings.failureMode: Both Basedpyright and Mypy exit nonzero because line 40 returns `str | None` as `str`, blocking the required style checks.
findings.title: Reject missing renderer results before returning

findings.description: The newly added mixed-list test places the literal on the left of `==`, triggering the repository's enabled Ruff SIM300 rule. `uv run --dev ruff check` exits 1 on this exact line, so the lint gate fails until the operands are swapped to `result.outputs["output"] == "1, two, 3.0, True"`.
findings.failureMode: The required Ruff check exits nonzero with SIM300 at the changed assertion, blocking the lint/merge check.
findings.title: Rewrite the Yoda assertion so Ruff passes

findings.description: The added signatures for `test_run_with_string_concatenation` (and the same split signature at lines 703–705) do not match Ruff's formatter output. `ruff format --check` exits 1 and reports this changed file would be reformatted, so the formatting gate fails; run the formatter so each signature uses the canonical single-line layout.
findings.failureMode: `uv run --dev ruff format --check` exits nonzero for the changed test file at the two added function signatures.
findings.title: Apply Ruff formatting to the added tests

findings.description: The new injection point selects the fallback with `template_renderer or ...`, so a valid renderer that implements falsy truthiness (for example via `__bool__` or `__len__`) is silently discarded. A workflow configured with that renderer then calls the sandbox-backed renderer instead, producing different output or a sandbox/network failure. Use an explicit `is not None` check here and at `TemplateTransformNode` line 41 so every object satisfying the renderer protocol is honored.
findings.failureMode: Passing a valid but falsy `Jinja2TemplateRenderer` causes the factory/node to replace it with `CodeExecutorJinja2TemplateRenderer`, so execution uses the wrong dependency and may fail on sandbox access.
findings.title: Preserve non-None renderers even when they are falsy

findings.description: All 23 newly added `test_*` functions were appended to `template_transform_node_spec.py`, but the repository invokes pytest on the `unit_tests` directory and no custom collection hook or `python_files` pattern includes `*_spec.py`. A directory-level `pytest --collect-only` for this package reports `no tests collected`, so none of these changed tests run in CI. Move the new cases into a valid `test_*.py` module (using the current workflow test fixtures) so they are collected and executed.
findings.failureMode: The API test job's directory-level pytest invocation silently collects zero tests from this changed module, so every added test is skipped.
findings.title: Move the added tests into a pytest-collected module

findings.description: This change grows the Python file from 414 lines to 1,151 lines, so the newly added section crosses the repository mandate that every Python file under `api/` remain below 800 lines. The resulting file is non-compliant and must be split into smaller test modules before merge.
findings.failureMode: The changed backend Python file violates the repository's mandatory under-800-line acceptance criterion and is rejected by compliance review.
findings.title: Split the backend test file below the mandated size cap

findings.description: Every newly added `test_run_*` definition from this line through `test_run_with_escape_filter` omits types for its parameters and return value. This violates the repository's mandatory rule that all Python function definitions include explicit annotations; annotate the fixture/mock parameters and add `-> None` to each added test.
findings.failureMode: The changed test module fails the repository's mandatory Python type-annotation acceptance criteria for each newly added function.
findings.title: Annotate the newly added Python test functions

findings.description: Wrapping `handleAction` in an unstructured `Task` defers synchronous forward actions. `OnboardingViewCompact.handleBottomButtonAction` consequently returns and posts `.screenChanged` while the old card is still selected; `pageCount` changes only after the main actor yields, with no later focus notification. With VoiceOver enabled this can focus or announce the outgoing card rather than the newly selected one. The callback is already `@MainActor`, so call `onboardingService.handleAction` directly instead of adding a task boundary.
findings.failureMode: With VoiceOver enabled, tapping a forward onboarding button posts the accessibility screen-change notification before the Task advances `pageCount`, creating a reachable stale-focus ordering hazard.
findings.title: Keep forward-card completion synchronous with the tap handler

findings.description: This changed constraint inlines the UI measurement `40` after the diff deletes `DownloadToast.UX.buttonSize` (the same literal is also used for the adjacent height constraint). The repository explicitly classifies scattered UI measurement literals as a compliance failure. Restore a private nested `UX.buttonSize` constant and use it for both constraints.
findings.failureMode: The changed Swift file fails the mandatory UI-constant organization contract because a layout measurement is scattered as literals instead of being defined in the required nested UX namespace.
findings.title: Keep the button size in the component's UX constants

findings.description: This source literal emits `ESCAPE '\\'` with two backslash characters inside the SQL string. Each ClickZetta connection is explicitly switched to `quote` string-literal escape mode, where backslashes are not collapsed by the string parser, while `ESCAPE` requires a single character. If `MATCH_ALL` raises one of the handled errors and calls `_search_by_like`, the fallback query is rejected instead of returning documents. Emit one backslash between the SQL quotes (or use another confirmed single-character escape).
findings.failureMode: A handled ClickZetta full-text-search failure turns into an unhandled SQL error in the LIKE fallback.
findings.title: Emit a single-character ClickZetta escape literal

findings.description: `WorkflowRun.inputs` and `outputs` are text columns written using default `json.dumps`, so a value such as `中文` is stored as `\u4e2d\u6587`. The removed expression deliberately converted the search term to that representation (and doubled the slash for LIKE), whereas the new helper leaves non-ASCII text unchanged; searching workflow logs for `中文` now silently returns zero matching runs. Preserve the Unicode-to-JSON conversion before applying LIKE escaping.
findings.failureMode: Workflow log keyword search silently returns no matching runs for non-ASCII input/output text.
findings.title: Preserve JSON Unicode encoding in workflow-log search

findings.description: `escape_like_pattern` prefixes `%`, `_`, and `\` with backslash, but this fallback SQL declares `|` as the escape character. With `IRIS_TEXT_INDEX` disabled, searching for literal `50%` therefore sends `%50\%%` under `ESCAPE '|'`: IRIS looks for a literal backslash and leaves `%` active instead of matching the stored `50%`, so the intended document is missed. Declare backslash in the SQL or escape the pattern with `|`.
findings.failureMode: IRIS fallback full-text search returns wrong results for queries containing `%`, `_`, or `\`.
findings.title: Use the same escape character in the IRIS LIKE clause

findings.description: The new local `SlotInfo` declares `fromUser.id` as `string`, but the response is produced from `IFromUser`, whose `id` is a number, and the mapper assigns `user.id` directly. This also makes the hook's `schedule.data` incompatible with existing consumers such as `useAvailableTimeSlots`, which accepts `IGetAvailableSlots`; if emitted/transpiled anyway, public-hook consumers can type-check string operations and then receive a number at runtime. Declare this field as `number` to preserve the server response contract.
findings.failureMode: The atoms TypeScript build rejects the changed hook response at consumers expecting `IGetAvailableSlots`; consumers compiling only against the public declaration can instead crash when performing string operations on the numeric runtime ID.
findings.title: Keep `fromUser.id` numeric in the copied slot response

findings.description: The replacement response type declares `availability.days` as `string[]`, but Prisma's `Availability.days` is `Int[]` and the existing schedule-list transformer requires `number[]`. As a result, `ListSchedulesPlatformWrapper` now passes the hook result to `getScheduleListItemData` with an incompatible type and the atoms TypeScript build fails. Preserve the handler contract with `days: number[]`.
findings.failureMode: Building/type-checking the atoms package fails at the unchanged `getScheduleListItemData(schedule)` call because the changed local response type says `days` contains strings rather than numbers.
findings.title: Type schedule availability days as numbers

findings.description: The new export points at `./booker/types.ts`, but this package's `files` allowlist only publishes `dist`, CSS, and fonts. `npm pack --dry-run` confirms that `booker/types.ts` is absent from the tarball, so a consumer using the newly introduced `import type { Slot } from "@calcom/atoms/booker/types"` cannot resolve the module after publication. Generate/target a declaration under `dist` or include the source file in the published files.
findings.failureMode: After publishing @calcom/atoms, downstream TypeScript builds importing the new booker/types subpath fail with a module-not-found error because the export target is not in the package tarball.
findings.title: Publish the new `booker/types` export target

findings.description: The moved type changes `userIds` from `number[]` to `string[]`, even though the source type and slot-generation types define user IDs as numbers. Existing `Booker` consumers that explicitly type the public `onTimeslotsLoaded` callback with the prior numeric slot shape will no longer be assignable and fail TypeScript compilation after this update. Copy the original `number[]` contract unchanged.
findings.failureMode: A downstream Booker integration whose onTimeslotsLoaded callback handles numeric user IDs, as permitted before this change, fails to compile against the updated props.
findings.title: Preserve numeric `userIds` in the moved `Slot` type

findings.description: The broadened restriction now rejects every `@calcom/trpc/**` import, but two atoms components still import `@calcom/trpc/components/QueryCell`. With this configuration, linting either component exits nonzero with `noRestrictedImports`, leaving the package unable to satisfy the new rule when those files are checked. Migrate those remaining imports as part of this change rather than enabling the all-TRPC ban while violations remain.
findings.failureMode: Biome lint fails on both remaining QueryCell imports whenever those atoms components are checked.
findings.title: Migrate the remaining atoms TRPC imports before banning them

findings.description: The new validation helper uses single-quoted strings despite the repository's Biome configuration requiring double quotes. Running `biome check packages/platform/atoms/hooks/schedules/types.ts` exits 1 on these lines, so the repository's required formatting validation fails until this file is formatted.
findings.failureMode: Biome's formatting validation exits nonzero for the changed file.
findings.title: Format the new schedule types file with Biome

findings.description: `updateActionStack` sets each newly inserted button's alpha to 0, but this concatenation now appends `browserActionStack` twice and omits `trailingPageActionStack`. The normal loaded-page state adds reload/stop and sometimes reader/summarize as trailing actions, so on the toolbar's first configuration these controls stay transparent and cannot be tapped. Replace the second browser stack with `trailingPageActionStack.arrangedSubviews`.
findings.failureMode: On first configuration of a loaded page, trailing reload/stop/reader/summarize controls remain transparent and unavailable.
findings.title: Restore trailing actions to the fade-in list

findings.description: With tab swiping enabled, the right skeleton starts at the container's trailing edge and extends almost a full container width to the right. This changed constraint puts the live toolbar's leading edge at that skeleton's far edge while its trailing edge remains at the skeleton's near edge, reversing the toolbar edges and yielding an unsatisfiable/negative-width layout. Restore `leftSkeletonAddressBar.trailingAnchor` as the leading anchor.
findings.failureMode: Enabling swiping tabs creates a reversed-width live address toolbar, causing constraint breakage and a collapsed or displaced URL bar.
findings.title: Anchor the toolbar between the skeleton bars

findings.description: The divider sits directly before `trailingPageActionStack`, but this renamed predicate now inspects the leading stack. A caller using the public default UX configuration (which requests a 4-point divider) with trailing-only page actions gets a zero-width/missing separator; a leading-only configuration can show a separator beside an empty trailing region. Check `trailingPageActionStack.arrangedSubviews`, preserving the renamed stack's old behavior.
findings.failureMode: A default-UX toolbar with trailing-only page actions renders without its configured divider.
findings.title: Base divider visibility on trailing actions

findings.description: After `SelectLightTheme`, the test reads `darkThemeView` and expects it to be selected. The action actually taps `lightThemeView`, so in the normal successful state the queried dark control remains `"0"` and `testCheckSystemThemeChanges` fails immediately. Read `lightThemeView` here instead.
findings.failureMode: Running `testCheckSystemThemeChanges` with theme selection working correctly produces an XCTest assertion failure immediately after selecting Light mode.
findings.title: Check the selected light-theme control

findings.description: The newly reordered navigation now occurs only after `Done` is tapped, but tapping the Shortcuts row pushes `TopSitesSettingsViewController`. That controller defines no Done item; `Done` belongs to the underlying `HomePageSettingViewController`. Consequently the preceding `waitAndTap()` waits for a nonexistent button and the functional test fails. Navigate/back out of Shortcuts before trying to tap Done.
findings.failureMode: Running `testDisableTopSitesSettingsRemovesSection` reaches the Shortcuts settings page, disables the switch, then times out waiting for Done before either absence assertion.
findings.title: Back out of Shortcuts before tapping Done

findings.description: Deleting `checkCopiedUrl()` removes the only assertion of the copied value reached by this test on supported iOS 15, because the replacement paste-and-compare block is guarded by `#available(iOS 17, *)`. If Copy writes an empty or wrong URL on iOS 15, `testClipboard` now passes after only driving the UI. Restore the iOS-15 clipboard validation (or explicitly skip that platform instead of reporting success).
findings.failureMode: On iOS 15, a regression where Copy writes the wrong URL no longer fails `testClipboard`; the test completes without checking clipboard content.
findings.title: Preserve clipboard validation on iOS 15

findings.description: `checkUrl`, `copyUrl`, and `checkCopiedUrl` are implementation helpers with no callers outside this test class, yet all three are changed to `public`. This violates the repository's mandatory minimal-access rule (which expressly treats APIs marked public when only used internally as a failure) and needlessly adds undocumented public declarations. Keep these helpers private/internal rather than publishing them.
findings.failureMode: The changed file fails the repository's mandatory access-control/public-API compliance gate by exposing three implementation-only methods as public APIs without documentation.
findings.title: Do not publish test-only clipboard helpers

findings.description: Changing this helper from `std::io::Result` to `Result<_, FileWriteError>` breaks every `?` call in `prepare_tools`: that function returns `crate::Result`, but `crate::Error` has no `From<FileWriteError>` implementation or variant. Linux builds of `tauri-bundler` therefore fail with E0277 before any bundling can run. Restore `std::io::Result` (or explicitly add/map a compatible crate error).
findings.failureMode: Compiling tauri-bundler for Linux fails at the `write_and_make_executable(...)?` call sites because the new private error cannot be converted into `crate::Error`.
findings.title: Return an error type accepted by the callers

findings.description: `write_and_make_executable` now calls `set_permissions` before creating the file. All fresh-cache callers invoke it specifically for a path that does not exist, so the first AppImage build returns `NotFound` while preparing AppRun/linuxdeploy/plugins. Write the bytes first, then chmod the created file.
findings.failureMode: Any AppImage bundle with at least one missing cached tool aborts during `prepare_tools` before linuxdeploy runs.
findings.title: Write new tool files before setting their permissions

findings.description: The existence check is inverted. With the normal empty tools cache, this block skips writing `linuxdeploy-plugin-gtk.sh`, but every AppImage build later invokes `linuxdeploy --plugin gtk`; linuxdeploy therefore cannot locate the required plugin and the bundle fails. Change the condition back to `if !gtk.exists()`.
findings.failureMode: An AppImage build using a fresh tools directory reaches linuxdeploy without a GTK plugin executable and fails instead of producing the bundle.
findings.title: Create the inlined GTK plugin when it is absent

findings.description: `FileWriteError` is a newly introduced custom error type, but these changed lines manually implement `Display` and `Error`. That directly violates the repository's mandatory structured-error rule requiring custom enums to use `#[derive(thiserror::Error)]` with `#[error(...)]` attributes, so the change fails repository compliance even if its separate conversion error is fixed. Derive `thiserror::Error` instead of maintaining these manual implementations (or keep the prior `io::Result` and remove the custom type).
findings.failureMode: The PR is rejected by the repository's mandatory error-handling compliance gate/review because the new custom enum manually implements the traits forbidden by the rule.
findings.title: Derive the custom error with thiserror

findings.description: The required `cargo fmt --all -- --check` job rewrites this 101-column statement into a two-line chain, so the repository's formatting gate fails on this change. Apply rustfmt to the file.
findings.failureMode: The mandatory Rust formatting CI check fails and blocks the change from passing validation.
findings.title: Format the new Rust statement

findings.description: Both newly added plugin scripts are consistently indented with four spaces (for example here and at `linuxdeploy-plugin-gstreamer.sh:7`), while the repository's mandatory EditorConfig sets `indent_size = 2` for every file. Reindent both scripts to two spaces so the added sources pass repository compliance.
findings.failureMode: The new source files fail the repository's mandatory EditorConfig compliance review because their block indentation does not match the required two spaces.
findings.title: Use the mandated two-space indentation in the inlined scripts

findings.description: A normal reader-mode toolbar tap dispatches `showReaderMode`, but this reducer now maps that action to `.readerModeLongPressAction`. BrowserViewController handles that state by creating a reading-list record, whereas `.readerMode` calls the actual enable/disable toggle. Consequently every ordinary tap adds the article to Reading List (or shows its error/duplicate result) instead of entering or leaving reader mode. Keep `.readerMode` here; only `handleAddToReadingListLongPressAction` should produce the long-press state.
findings.failureMode: On any reader-capable page, tapping the reader-mode toolbar button performs add-to-reading-list behavior and reader mode does not toggle.
findings.title: Restore the normal reader-mode display action

findings.description: A reader-mode tab's raw URL is an `http://localhost/.../reader-mode/page` URL, and `cancelEditMode` now forwards it because reader URLs also satisfy `isWebPage()`. The normal URL update stores `tab.url?.displayURL` (the original article), but the cancel reducer prefers this non-nil raw action URL, and LocationView renders its `absoluteString`. Thus canceling edit/opening menu or tabs in reader mode replaces the visible article URL with Firefox's internal localhost URL. Preserve the `!currentURL.isReaderModeURL` exclusion or pass `currentURL.displayURL`.
findings.failureMode: While viewing an article in reader mode, enter address-bar edit mode and cancel it (or tap a control that calls cancelEditMode); the location field displays Firefox's internal localhost reader URL instead of the article URL.
findings.title: Keep internal reader URLs out of the address bar

findings.description: The new branches reverse the transition documented by the inline comment and metric schema: tapping `.available` opens reader mode and should yield enabled=true, while tapping `.active` closes it and should yield false. With the code as written, the pre-existing extra-key argument swap makes this change visibly regress `is_private` too: an active normal tab is recorded as private, and an available private tab as non-private. Nil/default state also makes the existing non-private middleware test fail. Restore the original true/false mapping; the separate pre-existing key swap is outside this diff.
findings.failureMode: Reader-mode tap telemetry is misclassified for reachable active/available states, and the existing default-state test receives `savedExtras.isPrivate == true` instead of false.
findings.title: Do not invert reader-mode telemetry state

findings.description: A path cannot have both `json` and `json5` as its extension, so validation is skipped for every JSON configuration. This removes the schema-only `productName` path-character check while serde stores the value as a plain string; on Linux AppImage builds that value is joined into `output_path`, and `create_dir(..., true)` recursively removes an existing directory before recreating it. A config such as `productName: "../victim"` can therefore delete `victim.AppDir` adjacent to the bundle output instead of being rejected. Restore `||` so both formats are validated.
findings.failureMode: Building an AppImage from JSON/JSON5 with a traversal `productName` can recursively delete an existing directory outside the AppImage output directory.
findings.title: Keep JSON schema validation reachable

findings.description: The schema and `Config` place `identifier` at the root, whereas `bundle` is an object. For every normal mobile config, `as_str()` on `bundle` produces `None`; all four Android/iOS build and dev entry points call `write_options`, which then returns `app configuration is missing an identifier` before launching the IDE build. Keep reading `config.get("identifier")`.
findings.failureMode: Every valid Android or iOS dev/build invocation fails while writing CLI options because `original_identifier()` is always `None`.
findings.title: Read the original identifier from the top level

findings.description: After merging into the temporary `value`, the new code only records the patch in `extensions` and drops `value`; it no longer deserializes the merged value into `config_metadata.inner`, despite `merge_with`'s contract. A caller that loads config and then invokes `merge_with` receives an unchanged dereferenced `Config`, so options such as an overridden `build.devUrl` retain the old value. Restore the assignment to `config_metadata.inner` before recording the extension.
findings.failureMode: Calling `merge_with` on a loaded configuration returns success but subsequent reads through the returned handle ignore the requested overrides.
findings.title: Commit the merged value back into the loaded config

findings.description: The required `cargo fmt --all -- --check` fails: rustfmt splits both the long schema parsing statement here and the new `config_metadata.extensions.insert(...)` chain at line 289. Commit the rustfmt output for both changed sites.
findings.failureMode: The mandatory Rust formatting check exits nonzero on the changed config file.
findings.title: Run rustfmt on the new config code

findings.description: The `<=` iteration executes once with `j == numkeys`, so every keyed cluster-mode command reads `keys_result->keys[numkeys]` and writes `slot_buffer[numkeys]` past the allocated buffer. For up to six keys, `GETKEYS_RESULT_INIT` leaves that extra key entry zeroed, so the function additionally hashes `argv[0]` and commonly rejects even a valid single-key command as CROSSSLOT; for larger results the out-of-bounds key-position read can index outside `argv`. In all cases the heap write can corrupt memory or crash the server. Iterate while `j < keys_result->numkeys`.
findings.failureMode: A routine cluster-mode keyed command is spuriously rejected and performs an out-of-bounds heap write; larger crafted commands can also cause an invalid argv access and server crash.
findings.title: Stop at the last extracted key

findings.description: The new `malloc` and both `free` calls resolve to declarations explicitly marked deprecated in `server.h`. Consequently the mandated `make REDIS_CFLAGS="-Werror"` build fails while compiling `cluster.c` with three `-Wdeprecated-declarations` errors, so this revision cannot pass the required build. Use `zmalloc`/`zfree` (or remove the unused buffer).
findings.failureMode: The required warnings-as-errors build fails to compile cluster.c due to direct malloc/free calls.
findings.title: Replace direct allocation calls with Redis wrappers

findings.description: `write_and_make_executable` now returns `FileWriteError`, but every caller is inside `prepare_tools`, whose error type is `crate::Error`; `crate::Error` has no `From<FileWriteError>` variant or implementation. Consequently every `?` on this helper is rejected with E0277 when the Linux module is compiled. Return the existing `std::io::Result` or explicitly convert/attach this structured error to `crate::Error`.
findings.failureMode: The Linux tauri-bundler build/clippy job fails to compile at each `write_and_make_executable(...)?` call with E0277.
findings.title: Return an error type accepted by `prepare_tools`

findings.description: The helper now calls `set_permissions` before `fs::write` has created the path. `download` only returns a `Vec<u8>` and does not create the target, while the inlined bytes are also memory-only. On a clean cache, therefore, the first missing `AppRun-*` causes `set_permissions` to return `NotFound` and AppImage bundling aborts. Restore write-then-chmod ordering.
findings.failureMode: Any first AppImage build with an empty tools directory fails while preparing the first missing tool with an ENOENT permissions error.
findings.title: Write new tool files before setting permissions

findings.description: The existence guard was inverted while replacing the download. A fresh tools directory skips creation of `linuxdeploy-plugin-gtk.sh`, yet every AppImage invocation requests `--plugin gtk`, so linuxdeploy cannot locate the required plugin and bundling fails. Change this back to `if !gtk.exists()` (or unconditionally refresh it).
findings.failureMode: After the other tool files are prepared in a clean cache, a normal AppImage build reaches linuxdeploy without the GTK plugin and fails plugin discovery.
findings.title: Install the GTK plugin when it is missing

findings.description: The required `cargo fmt --all -- --check` job reports a diff on this newly added `set_permissions(...).map_err(...)` line. Apply rustfmt's split-line output so the mandatory formatting check passes.
findings.failureMode: The repository's rustfmt CI job fails and blocks the merge.
findings.title: Format the new helper before merge

findings.description: The newly introduced custom error manually implements `Display` and `std::error::Error`, contrary to the repository's mandatory structured-error rule requiring custom error enums to derive `thiserror::Error` with `#[error(...)]` messages. Converting this enum to the required derive also provides a clean place to add the conversion needed by `prepare_tools`.
findings.failureMode: The change fails the repository's mandatory error-type compliance review and leaves error formatting/conversion outside the standardized `thiserror` mechanism.
findings.title: Derive the custom error with `thiserror`

findings.description: Both newly added shell sources use four-space block indentation (for example here and throughout `linuxdeploy-plugin-gtk.sh`), while the repository-wide EditorConfig and mandatory source-file rule require two spaces for every file type. Reindent both inlined scripts to two spaces.
findings.failureMode: The newly committed source files fail the repository's mandatory EditorConfig compliance review.
findings.title: Use the repository's two-space indentation in inlined scripts

findings.description: This changed require now targets `lib/magic-link/magic-link`, but the head tree still contains only `lib/magic-link/MagicLink.js`. Loading the members API therefore throws `MODULE_NOT_FOUND`; `members.init()` loads `services/members/api.js`, which imports this module, so normal service startup cannot initialize members. Restore the require to the existing `MagicLink` path.
findings.failureMode: The normal boot call to members.init() rejects with MODULE_NOT_FOUND before the members service can initialize.
findings.title: Use the existing MagicLink filename

findings.description: The wrapper now requires `../email-service/email-event-storage`, but that service was not renamed and the head tree contains only `EmailEventStorage.js`. `boot.js` calls this wrapper's `init()`, so startup reaches this require and throws `MODULE_NOT_FOUND`. findings.title: Use the existing EmailEventProcessor filename

findings.description: Nine changed `const ... = require(...)` declarations in lines 1-10 now omit their terminating semicolons. This violates the repository's explicit-semicolon source rule and causes the lint check for this production module to fail; retain the kebab-case paths but restore the semicolons.

findings.description: These changed constraints hard-code the `40`-point close-button size after deleting `struct UX { static let buttonSize: CGFloat = 40 }`. That directly violates the repository mandate that UI measurements be defined in a component's nested `UX` struct, so this file fails the mandatory compliance gate. Restore a private `UX.buttonSize` constant and use it for both dimensions.
findings.failureMode: The modified UI component is rejected by the mandatory repository compliance gate because its close-button measurement is now hard-coded outside a nested UX struct.
findings.title: Keep the button size in the nested UX struct

findings.description: New trailing actions are initialized with alpha 0, but this list now appends browserActionStack a second time instead of trailingPageActionStack. On the initial URL configuration, the reload/reader actions therefore remain invisible in both animated and non-animated paths. Restore trailingPageActionStack.arrangedSubviews as the final term.
findings.failureMode: Open a URL whose toolbar adds reload or reader-mode as a new trailing action; the action remains at alpha 0 and is not displayed.
findings.title: Restore alpha for trailing page actions

findings.description: With tab swiping enabled, rightSkeletonAddressBar begins at the container's trailing edge and extends farther right. Using that bar's trailing edge for toolbar.leading while using its leading edge for toolbar.trailing reverses the toolbar's horizontal anchors, causing a broken/collapsed address-bar layout and constraint conflicts. Restore leftSkeletonAddressBar.trailingAnchor for the leading constraint.
findings.failureMode: Initialize AddressToolbarContainer with isSwipingTabsEnabled true; the main toolbar is constrained backward across the offscreen right skeleton instead of across the container.
findings.title: Anchor the toolbar between both skeleton bars

findings.description: The divider is constrained immediately before trailingPageActionStack, but the renamed check now tests leadingPageActionStack. A configuration with trailing actions and no leading actions forces the expected divider width to zero; a leading-only configuration can instead show a stray divider. Check trailingPageActionStack, matching the pre-rename pageActionStack behavior.
findings.failureMode: Configure BrowserAddressToolbar with AddressToolbarUXConfiguration.default(), one trailing page action, and no leading page action; the expected divider between the URL and trailing action disappears.
findings.title: Base divider visibility on trailing actions

findings.description: `result.get("result")` is `str | None`, and the guard explicitly permits `None` before returning it from a method declared to return `str`. The registered `make type-check` command fails with `reportReturnType` on this changed line. Reject every non-string value with `TemplateRenderError` so the implementation actually returns `str`.

Both repository type-checkers reject the changed file at this line (`uv run --dev basedpyright ...` and the CI Mypy command each exit nonzero), so the style gate cannot pass. findings.description: The new injection point selects the fallback with `template_renderer or ...`, so a valid renderer that implements falsy truthiness (for example via `__bool__` or `__len__`) is silently discarded. A workflow configured with that renderer then calls the sandbox-backed renderer instead, producing different output or a sandbox/network failure. Use an explicit `is not None` check here and at `TemplateTransformNode` line 41 so every object satisfying the renderer protocol is honored.
findings.failureMode: Passing a valid but falsy `Jinja2TemplateRenderer` causes the factory/node to replace it with `CodeExecutorJinja2TemplateRenderer`, so execution uses the wrong dependency and may fail on sandbox access.
findings.title: Preserve non-None renderers even when they are falsy
